scene.world: World: gravity, air resistance, body thickness, ground, pace
scene.worldGravity: Gravitational acceleration in m/s² (Earth 9.81, Moon 1.62, 0 — weightlessness)
scene.worldAir: Air resistance: 1 — normal, 0 — vacuum, more — denser air
scene.worldDepth: Body thickness in metres (with density and area it gives the mass); usually 0.1
scene.worldGround: false — no ground (a table seen from above, space)
scene.worldSpeed: Pace of time at the start (1 — as in reality)
scene.vars: Values drawn at every opening (and with „New draw”) — used in expressions "=…" and in texts as "{nazwa}" (nazwa = the value’s name)
scene.varsPick: Instead of a number: a list of texts to draw from (e.g. liquids)
scene.bodies: Bodies: balls, blocks, polygons — of a material or with their own density
scene.bodiesId: Body name (letters, digits, - _) — in joints, goal and graph
scene.bodiesX: Position of the centre (poly: of the origin of its points) in metres
scene.bodiesPoints: Polygon points [[x, y], …] relative to x, y
scene.bodiesMaterial: Material: wood, oak, cork, steel, aluminium, lead, gold, rubber, ice, stone, plastic, glass, paper, foam, ball, egg
scene.bodiesDensity: Own density in kg/m³ (instead of the material’s)
scene.bodiesTrace: true — draws a trace of its motion
scene.joints: Joints: pivot, rod, rope, spring, pulley
scene.jointsB: Second body (id) — omitted: attached to the world
scene.jointsAt: Point in the world (without "b") or on body "b"; for a pulley — the first wheel
scene.jointsOn: Point on body "a" relative to its centre (default: the centre)
scene.jointsLength: Length (default: how far apart the ends are)
scene.fluidsLayers: Layers of liquid from the bottom (a lighter one rises to the top by itself)
scene.fluidsLayersLiquid: Liquid: water, saltwater, sea, oil, alcohol, glycerin, honey, mercury, milk
scene.fluidsLayersHeight: Height of the layer in an empty tank (m)
scene.fluidsHoles: Holes in the walls (a jet following Torricelli’s law)
scene.fluidsHolesAt: Height above the bottom (with "bottom": distance from the left wall)
scene.show: What is visible: arrows, traces, grid, pressure, values
scene.showPressure: true — pressure in the liquid as a darker shade in the depth
scene.showValues: false — no labels of masses and forces
scene.graph: A graph over time for one body
scene.allowPalette: What can be added: ball, box, plank, wedge, ramp, wall, pendulum, spring, pulley, seesaw, basin
scene.allowTools: Tools: pin, rope, rod, link (spring), ruler, probe (pressure), delete
scene.allowEdit: false — no changing of materials and body settings
scene.goal: Goal: a body in an area for a while — then a message appears
scene.goalArea: Area [x0, y0, x1, y1] (numbers or expressions)
scene.goalFor: How many seconds it has to stay there
scene.goalSay: What to say when it succeeds
scene.steps: Steps of the experiment — „Show” performs them one by one
scene.stepsSay: What to do in this step
scene.stepsWait: How many seconds the step lasts with „Show”
scene.view: What is visible at the start: [x0, y0, x1, y1]

physics.use: A 2D physics lab: bodies of real materials, slopes, pendulums, springs, pulleys, collisions, liquids (pressure, buoyancy, communicating vessels, jets) — a sandbox or a ready school experiment; full screen.
physics.title: Physics lab
physics.showsStrip: {title} — a card with a button: the lab opens full screen.

key.title: Title of the experiment (above the scene)
key.text: Text for students — what they should do and observe (paragraphs)
key.mode: "experiment" — exactly this scene (with „Show”), "sandbox" — everything is allowed, ready experiments to load, saving and JSON export
key.scene: Scene: world, bodies, joints, tanks of liquid, pipes, what is visible, what is allowed, goal and steps — the engine is built in, the scene says what stands in it
key.question: in a story with a knowledge base: reaching the scene’s goal ("goal") counts as a correct answer to this question of the base — id or @name (empty: its own goal card)

scene.seed: Random seed — the same number, the same run (e.g. the pits in the walls where bubbles are born)
scene.box: Inside of the box in metres and the thickness of the 2D layer
scene.boxDepth: Layer thickness (m), usually 0.01 — masses and energies follow from it
scene.ambient: Surroundings: pressure, temperature, humidity, gravity, air composition
scene.ambientP: Pressure in kPa (101.325 — sea level; 70 — a high mountain; 200 — a pressure cooker)
scene.ambientRh: Relative humidity of the air, from 0 to 1
scene.ambientG: Gravitational acceleration in m/s², from 2.45 (1/4 g) to 19.6 (2 g)
scene.ambientAir: Composition of dry air — mass fractions, e.g. { "N2": 0.7676, "O2": 0.2324 }
scene.ambientAirN2: Mass fraction of nitrogen in the air
scene.ambientAirO2: Mass fraction of oxygen in the air
scene.sides: Each side of the box: "wall" or "open" (open to the room)
scene.quality: Cell size: "high" (2 mm, normal), "very-high" (1 mm, a strong computer), "medium" (3 mm, a weaker computer); a device on which someone chose another one keeps its own
scene.extremes: Violent phenomena (explosive boiling of superheated water, very fast water motion): "ask" (default — the lab stops and asks how to continue computing), "compute" (compute exactly, as in reality — water may fly out of the vessel), "normalize" (soften: bubbles at most 4 mm, no superheating, water stays in the vessel)
scene.ops: Build steps in order — the starting setup, not the run
scene.opsOp: "fill" (water or air), "erase" (remove — air comes back), "solid" (a fixed structure of cells), named objects with settings: "body" (a block, ice cube, stone — an exact rectangle: falls, floats, sinks, tips over; ice melts and freezes on with whole faces), "beaker", "hotplate"; "grains" (a handful of salt crystals: falls, sinks, piles up, dissolves); "move" (move object "id" together with its contents, or everything solid in an area), "remove" (take away object "id"); "pin" (older scenes: pin or unpin a body at point x, y — today "pinned" on the object)
scene.opsId: Object name ("body", "beaker", "hotplate"), e.g. "cube" — under it the lab selects the object and changes its settings in the object itself; in "move" and "remove" steps the name of the object they concern; without a name the object gets "body-1", "beaker-1" …
scene.opsDx: Horizontal shift (m) — in a "move" step; objects move exactly, painted structures by whole cells
scene.opsRegion: Area: rect, circle, poly or line with width; a body ("body") is always a rectangle — a circle becomes a square of the same area, a polygon the rectangle enclosing it, a line with width a rotated rectangle
scene.opsComposition: Composition (mass fractions): { "H2O": 1 } for water, { "oil-rapeseed": 1 } for rapeseed oil, { "H2O": 0.9, "NaCl": 0.1 } for 10 % brine (saturated is about 26 %), { "N2": 0.7676, "O2": 0.2324 } for air
scene.opsMaterial: Material: "glass" (borosilicate glass), "steel" (stainless steel), "ceramic" (boiling stones), "wood" (pine), "ice" (as a body it melts and freezes on, as a structure it does not), "stone" (granite); in a "grains" step: "NaCl" (table salt)
scene.opsD: Crystal diameter in a "grains" step (m): 0.0005 (default, table salt), from 0.00005 to 0.005 — finer ones sink more slowly and dissolve faster
scene.opsPinned: Object pinned (stays in place, does not fall) or free (false: falls under gravity); a block is free unless true; a beaker and a plate are pinned unless false — in the lab: the object’s „Pinned” field
scene.opsAngle: Rotation of the body in degrees anticlockwise (beaker and plate around the centre of the bottom, a body around the centre of its area)
scene.opsX: Centre of the apparatus (m); in a "pin" step the point of the body
scene.opsY: Bottom of the apparatus (m) — 0 is the bottom of the box; in a "pin" step the point of the body
scene.opsWall: Wall thickness of the beaker (m) — exact, the beaker is a body made of rectangles
scene.opsLid: true — a beaker with a tight lid (a closed gas region)
scene.opsPower: Plate power in W per layer thickness (with a thermostat: the maximum power)

lab2d.label: 2D lab
lab2d.use: 2D lab (engine v2): a box full of air in which you place beakers and hotplates and paint water — heat, convection, evaporation, boiling with bubbles, condensation and fog follow from the laws of physics and the materials database. Tools: probing a point, a bubble view with forces, overlays (temperature, pressure, velocity with arrows, humidity, vapour, phase map), a particle view, graphs, two levels. Full screen.

lab2d.showsStrip: {title} — a card with a button: the lab opens full screen.

choice.startBake: Bakes a recording right away (a ready one plays at once)

particles.label: Particle lab
particles.use: A 2D particle lab: a box full of air into which you paint water and place apparatus (beaker, hotplate) — the engine computes everything from local rules and the substance database. Stage M1a: mechanics (liquid and gas, walls, surface tension, buoyancy); heat and boiling in later stages. Full screen; the „All cores” button opens it in a new tab that computes on all cores.

shape.x: Position in drawing units (in a frame — world units): rect, image — top left corner (in a frame: bottom left); circle, ellipse — centre; text — anchor point; line, arrow — start; group, use — offset; frame — top left corner of the frame. A number or an expression "=…"
shape.r: circle — radius; rect — corner rounding (always in drawing units)
shape.d: path — an SVG path ("M10 10 L50 40 Z" …); in a frame it is not converted — use "poly" there
shape.text: text — the text; with values in {…}: "Angle: {fmt(kat, 0)}°"
shape.use: use — name of a part from "symbols"
shape.fill: Fill: a colour ("#rrggbb", "rgba(…)", "accent", "muted/35" …), "none", a glow "radial(rgba(120, 190, 255, 0.25), transparent 70%)" or an expression "=trafione ? 'ok' : 'accent'"
shape.glow: Glow/shadow: "x y blur colour", e.g. "0 0 10px rgba(160, 220, 255, 0.75)"
shape.origin: What it rotates and grows around: "center" (usual), "25% 75%" (part of the element), "170 225" (drawing units)
shape.rotate: group, use — rotation in degrees (in a frame: anticlockwise)
shape.children: group, frame — elements inside (the same keys)
shape.shift: group, use — the elements inside start moving this many ms later (e.g. successive cards 120 ms apart)
shape.motion: Motion of the element (described under: Motion) — an object or a list of up to three
shape.show: When the element is visible: an expression, e.g. "step >= 1" (second step of the scene) or "sily == 1"
shape.drag: Dragging: { "x": "variable" } — variable = finger position; { "set": { "kat": "deg(atan2(py, px))" } } — from the finger position (px, py); "label" — name of the handle
shape.dragX: Variable that receives the horizontal finger position
shape.dragY: Variable that receives the vertical finger position
shape.dragSet: Variables computed from the finger position: { "name": "expression with px, py" }
shape.dragLabel: Name of the handle for screen readers
shape.tapGo: In a presentation: where to — "next", "back", a scene key, "link:<id>"
shape.tapLabel: Name of the button for screen readers
shape.repeat: How many copies of the element (in each "i" = 0, 1, … and "n" = how many) — e.g. particles, a scale
shape.label: Name of the handle or button (dragging, clicking)
shape.head: arrow — size of the arrowhead (drawing units)
shape.points: poly — points [[x, y], …]: numbers or expressions "=…"
shape.fn: plot — y as an expression of "u" (e.g. "A*sin(2*pi*u/l)")
shape.fx: plot — x of the path from "u"; trace — what to follow horizontally (e.g. "x")
shape.fy: plot — y of the path from "u"; trace — what to follow vertically (e.g. "y")
shape.var: plot — name of the curve parameter (usually "u"; e.g. "i" for the zigzag of a spring)
shape.from: plot — from which parameter value (a number or "=…")
shape.to: plot — up to which parameter value (a number or "=…")
shape.samples: plot — from how many points (up to 600)
shape.keep: trace — how many of the latest points remain
shape.every: trace — a new point every this many seconds of simulation
shape.view: frame — which part of the world is visible: [x0, y0, x1, y1] (numbers or "=…"; y grows upwards)
shape.clip: frame — true: whatever leaves the frame disappears
shape.camera: frame — true: you can zoom (+, −, Ctrl+wheel, two fingers) and pan the view; "view" is then the „Fit” view
shape.typeMore: "group" gathers "children", "use" inserts a part from "symbols", "frame" is a frame with a world (y upwards), "world" — this is where the things of "world" stand (in a frame)

motion.delay: Delay (ms; in a loop it may be negative)
motion.from: From (a number, a point [x, y] or a colour)
motion.to: To (a number, a point [x, y] or a colour)
motion.path: move — the path: a list of points [x, y]
motion.length: draw outside a drawing — length of the stroke
motion.by: "scene", "enter" or "leave" — in a presentation the motion follows scrolling (the progress of the scene, its arrival or departure) instead of the clock

frame.draw: How much of the line is drawn (0–1)
frame.color: Colour of the fill or text
frame.reveal: How much is visible from the left (0–1)

vars.name: Name (letters, digits, _; does not start with a digit) — used in expressions
vars.step: Step of the slider and dragging
vars.label: Label at the slider
vars.random: At every opening (in Cogita: at every attempt) a random value from [from, to]

sim.stateRate: Rate of change — derivative over time (expression; e.g. "vy" for y, "-g" for vy)
sim.events: Events: when a condition BECOMES true
sim.eventsSetVy: e.g. the new velocity after a bounce — the key is the name of a quantity or variable
sim.speed: Pace relative to the clock (1 — as in reality)
sim.auto: true — starts by itself when the drawing is visible
sim.loop: true — starts again after the end
sim.sleep: true — when nothing moves any more, computing goes to sleep (saves battery) and wakes up at every change

controls.var: The variable it sets (slider, number, toggle, choice)
controls.label: Label (default: the variable’s label)
controls.go: button — in a presentation: "next", "back", a scene key, "link:<id>"
controls.show: When the element is visible — an expression (e.g. "solved": the „Next” button only after solving)

rules.when: Condition — the rule fires when it BECOMES true
rules.go: In a presentation: where next — "next", "back", a scene key, "link:<id>"
rules.goal: true — this is the goal of the task (in Cogita: a correct answer)
rules.for: How many seconds the condition must hold without a break before the rule fires (e.g. 1 — „steadily”)

predict.start: true (usual) — a task: the drawing starts paused, and every change after checking pauses it again; false — it runs at once, and the „Predict” button pauses it on request
predict.say: What is visible below the drawing while it is paused (e.g. „Set it as you think — then check”)
predict.check: Label of the button that lets it go (usually „Check”)
predict.again: Label of the button after checking that pauses it again (usually „Adjust”)
predict.hold: Label of the button that pauses on request (with "start": false; usually „Predict”)

task.require: Conditions of every drawn task (expressions) — e.g. "onstep(s, 0.5)" (result on the slider grid), "abs(s - r0) >= 1" (far enough from the start), "a != b"; the conditions alone decide on comparable difficulty
task.solve: The solution as expressions of the drawn values: "w2.pos = 3 + s; kat = 45" — it must be settable by hand; in Cogita the solution of the question, unless the question gives its own
task.new: Label of the „New task” button (false — no button); in Cogita every attempt draws anew anyway
task.tries: How many times at most to draw (usually 200); when nothing fits — the task from the values "value"

world.kinds: Kinds of things (up to 12): what each has, what follows from it, how it moves, how it looks and what may be done with it
world.kindsName: Name of the kind (like a variable name) — also a set in summaries: count(belka, !ok)
world.kindsLabel: Name for people („Beam”) — in the panel and on buttons
world.kindsProps: Properties (up to 24): numbers with limits — set in the panel, dragged, saved in the answer
world.kindsPropsName: Property name — in expressions of the thing „pos”, of the parent „parent.pos”, of the thing with a given id „w2.pos”
world.kindsPropsMin: Minimum — a number or an expression computed in the thing
world.kindsPropsMax: Maximum — a number or an expression, e.g. "=parent.length" (at most to the end of the beam it hangs on)
world.kindsPropsApart: Smallest distance from siblings in this property (two weights do not hang at one spot)
world.kindsPropsNew: Where a newly added thing stands — an expression, e.g. "parent.pivot + 1" (a free spot is found automatically)
world.kindsPropsWhen: When the property applies to this thing — an expression, e.g. "!isroot" (only when it hangs) or "isroot"
world.kindsPropsQuiet: true — do not show it among the data of the selected thing (e.g. the length of a string: it only changes the picture)
world.kindsLet: Values computed in every thing — the order follows from what they read (children first, then the parent, or the other way round)
world.kindsLetValue: Expression: own names, parent.x, root.x, sum(children, total*arm), count(…), names of the drawing (g, tol) and built-ins (isroot, depth, index, selected, nchildren)
world.kindsState: Simulation quantities of every thing — computed with the same Runge-Kutta as "sim" (then "dt", "speed", "auto", "sleep" are enough for "sim")
world.kindsStateRate: Rate of change — derivative over time (expression in the thing)
world.kindsEvents: Events of the thing: when a condition BECOMES true (e.g. a swing limiter)
world.kindsEventsWhen: Condition in the thing, e.g. "angle > tilt"
world.kindsEventsSet: New values of properties or quantities: { "angle": "tilt", "omega": 0 }
world.kindsEventsSay: Text below the drawing ({…} — computed in the thing)
world.kindsShapes: How the thing looks: elements as in "elements", computed in the thing ("=x" is ITS x); in a frame — world coordinates
world.kindsDrag: What dragging the thing sets: { "property": "expression with px, py" } — px, py is the finger in the world; the grab ring stands at its "x", "y"
world.kindsDragPos: E.g. a place: "px" (along the ground) or the projection of the finger onto the parent’s beam
world.kindsCan: What may be done with a thing of this kind
world.kindsCanEdit: Properties to set in the panel of the selected thing (slider, number, ±)
world.kindsCanAdd: Which kinds may be hung onto it
world.kindsCanRemove: true — it can be removed (together with what hangs on it)
world.kindsCanCopy: true — it can be duplicated (together with what hangs on it)
world.kindsReadouts: Readouts in the panel of the selected thing
world.kindsReadoutsShow: When the readout is visible — an expression, e.g. "!held" (not while the person is predicting)
world.kindsChildren: How many things at most may hang on it
world.kindsBrief: What the thing is called in the panel — a text with {…}, e.g. "{m} kg" („Weight 2 kg”); omitted — kind and id
world.kindsMark: true (usual) — a thing that may be changed has a dashed ring (when there are also given things); false — the kind shows it itself (colour, arrows: "can", "can.pos")
world.thingsId: Name of the thing (letters, digits, _ -) — in expressions „s1.pos”, in answers and in the Cogita solution („s1.pos = 4”)
world.thingsParent: What it hangs on (id); null or omitted — it stands at the very top
world.thingsLock: true — nothing may be changed or removed; a list — these properties may not be changed (a puzzle)
world.thingsPos: A property of the thing (any property of its kind, here "pos"): a number, { "random": [from, to] } (in Cogita drawn at every attempt) or an expression "=…" of the drawing’s values (random tasks: "=3 + s")
world.allow: What is allowed in this world at all — narrower than the kinds (a puzzle), never wider
world.allowEdit: true — properties may be set in the panel
world.allowRoots: Which kinds may be placed at the very top (e.g. a new stand)
world.keep: What must always hold — a change after which it no longer holds is undone
world.keepWhen: An expression, e.g. "edits <= 2" (at most two moves; edits — how many changes since „Start over”) or "nthings <= 6"
world.save: true — a workshop: „Save”, „Load” (in this browser) and the layout as JSON
world.hint: Hint below the drawing when nothing is selected ({…} — computed)
world.list: true — every property that may be changed as its own slider in the panel („You set”, without selecting a thing); false — select a thing first; omitted — rows, when nothing may be added or removed and there are at most 6 of them

animation.label: Animation
animation.use: A drawing that moves or can be moved: shapes, lines, graphs, vectors — with motion, sliders, dragging and a physics simulation (e.g. a throw, a pendulum, a spring). Also the pictures of the Cogita show.
animation.promptCopied: AI prompt copied — paste it in your chat, and the finished JSON here.
animation.hint: Drawing: „size”, „elements” (rect, circle, ellipse, line, arrow, poly, plot, trace, frame, path, text, image, group, use), „symbols”; for moving: „vars”, „let”, „sim”, „controls”, „rules”, and things to build (scales, gears) — „world” with a „world” element in a frame; values can be expressions „=…”. Full description — with the page JSON import and in the AI prompt. Now: {sum}.
animation.exampleLoaded: Example „{title}” — check the preview and accept.
animation.missing: The drawing has no element yet.
animation.showsMoving: Drawing ({sum}) in motion, across the full width of the module.
animation.showsLive: Drawing ({sum}) in motion, across the full width of the module, with controls below.

lead.do: What it does with the simulation
lead.buttonDo: button — what it does with the simulation

key.alt: Description of the drawing for screen readers (empty — the drawing is decorative only)
key.question: in a story with a knowledge base: the drawing’s goal (a rule with "goal": true) counts as a correct answer to this question of the base — id or @name (empty: its own goal card)
key.about: in a story with a knowledge base: for which entries of the base the reached goal of the drawing counts — id or @name, each on its own line
key.size: Size of the drawing in its own units: [width, height] — the drawing grows and shrinks as a whole with the module
key.max: At most this width in rem (a number); omitted — the full width of the module
key.panel: Where the controls go: "below" (below the drawing, usual) or "side" (beside it, when the drawing is wide; on a phone always below)
key.let: Values computed from others, in every frame, in this order: [{ "name", "value": "expression" }]
key.controls: Controls below the drawing: sliders, switches, choices, buttons, readouts
key.rules: Rules: when a condition becomes true — a text, the goal of the task, a setting, start/pause, onwards in a presentation
key.predict: Predict first, then see: the drawing stands still (simulation paused, rules silent, "held" = 1 in expressions — e.g. a colour that would give away the result waits) until the person clicks „Check”; "tries" — how many times they have checked. true or { "start", "say", "check", "again", "hold" }
key.task: A different task every time, equally hard: draws values from "random" (variables, properties of things, also as expressions of them) until the conditions hold, the task is not solved at the start, and the solution can be set. { "require", "solve", "new", "tries" }
key.world: A world of things to build (scales of beams and weights, gears): kinds, things at the start and what is allowed — every change goes through the rules of the world, with „Undo”; an element { "type": "world" } in a frame shows where they stand
key.symbols: Reusable parts: [{ "name": "fiszka", "shapes": [elements] }] — an element { "type": "use", "use": "fiszka" } inserts them
key.elements: Elements of the drawing, from back to front — each with position, look, motion ("motion") and — for moving — expressions, "drag", "tap", "show", "repeat"
